questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: Chemistry does not study the energy changes associated with chemical reactions.
questions.explanation: False. Chemistry is the study of matter, its properties, how substances combine or separate, and the energy changes that accompany chemical reactions.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: Analytical chemistry is only concerned with producing chemicals, not analyzing them.
questions.explanation: False. Analytical chemistry is specifically focused on identifying, separating, and quantifying the chemical components of natural and artificial materials.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: Industrial processes such as brewing, soap making, and dye production rely on chemical principles.
questions.explanation: True. Fermentation in brewing, saponification in soap making, and chemical synthesis of dyes are all direct applications of chemical principles.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: True or False: All measurements in chemistry must include a number and a unit.
questions.explanation: True. A physical quantity without a unit is meaningless in scientific measurements (e.g., stating a mass is "5" has no meaning without grams, kilograms, etc.).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The primary focus of chemistry is the study of:
options: The motion and forces affecting objects
The composition, structure, properties, and changes of matter
The history and evolution of the universe
questions.explanation: Option C is the fundamental definition of chemistry taught in Grade 9: the branch of natural science dealing with the composition, structure, properties, and reactions of matter.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the "matter" that chemists study?
options: Only the substances that can be seen and touched
Any substance that has mass and takes up space
Only the elements found on the Periodic Table
Only complex compounds, such as plastics and medicines
questions.explanation: Matter is scientifically defined as anything that possesses mass and occupies physical space (volume).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A chemist who is studying the rate at which a chemical reaction occurs is working in the branch of chemistry known as:
questions.explanation: Chemical kinetics and reaction rates, along with thermodynamics and quantum mechanics, belong directly to Physical Chemistry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The process of observing a substance and determining its components and their relative amounts is primarily the focus of which branch of chemistry?
questions.explanation: Analytical chemistry specializes in qualitative analysis (what is present) and quantitative analysis (how much is present).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A researcher is studying a newly discovered compound containing only carbon and hydrogen atoms. This falls under the branch of chemistry called:
questions.explanation: Organic chemistry is dedicated specifically to carbon-containing compounds, especially hydrocarbons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In industrial production, chemistry plays a critical role in converting raw materials into useful products such as:
options: Solar panels, wind turbines, and hydropower stations
Computer software, mobile apps, and video games
questions.explanation: Chemical industries synthesize polymers (plastics), pharmaceuticals (medicines), and agrochemicals (fertilizers) from petroleum and mineral raw materials.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In agriculture, chemistry is primarily used to:
options: Develop fertilizers and pesticides that increase crop yield
questions.explanation: Agricultural chemistry provides chemical fertilizers (like urea and DAP) and pesticides/herbicides to optimize crop production.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Petrochemical industries rely on chemistry mainly to:
options: Refine crude oil into fuels and useful chemical products
questions.explanation: The petrochemical industry uses fractional distillation and catalytic cracking to refine crude petroleum into fuels, lubricants, and polymer precursors.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following best defines the chemical industry?
options: The industry that produces machines and mechanical tools
The industry that extracts minerals from the earth
The industry that converts raw materials into useful products through chemical processes
The industry that provides banking and financial services
questions.explanation: A chemical industry uses chemical reactions and transformations to manufacture finished commercial goods from basic raw substances.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major sector of the chemical industry?
questions.explanation: Automobile repair is a service and mechanical maintenance sector, not a manufacturing branch of the chemical industry.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a chemical product?
options: Crude oil directly from the ground
Plastic made from polymerization of ethene
questions.explanation: Polyethylene plastic is an engineered synthetic product produced through the chemical polymerization reaction of ethene monomers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The composition of matter refers to:
options: The types and proportions of atoms or elements that make up a substance
The amount of energy matter contains
questions.explanation: Composition describes the elemental identity and relative proportions of the atoms that constitute a substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is not a basic physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Concentration (e.g. mol/L) is a derived quantity, whereas mass (kg), length (m), and thermodynamic temperature (K) are base SI quantities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Temperature in the SI system is measured in:
questions.explanation: The Kelvin (K) is the official SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following quantities measures the space occupied by matter?
questions.explanation: Volume is the physical measure of the three-dimensional space occupied by matter.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a derived physical quantity in chemistry?
questions.explanation: Density is derived from mass divided by volume (kg/m³), whereas time, mass, and amount of substance are base SI quantities.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: A chemist measures 2.5 mol of oxygen gas. The term mole refers to:
questions.explanation: The mole is the SI unit for amount of substance and represents a specific count of elementary entities (Avogadro's number, 6.022 × 10²³ particles).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Temperature is a measure of:
options: The total energy of a system
The average kinetic energy of particles in a substance
questions.explanation: Temperature is directly proportional to the average translational kinetic energy of the atoms or molecules in a substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which statement about the Kelvin scale is true?
options: It is based on the freezing and boiling points of water
It begins at absolute zero where all molecular motion stops
It is used only in meteorology
questions.explanation: The Kelvin absolute temperature scale starts at 0 K (absolute zero, -273.15 °C), where classical molecular thermal motion ceases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Convert 0 °C to Fahrenheit.
questions.explanation: Using the conversion formula °F = (°C × 9/5) + 32: (0 × 9/5) + 32 = 32 °F.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: If a sample of gas is heated from 27 °C to 327 °C, by how many Kelvin does the temperature increase?
questions.explanation: Because a change of 1 °C is equal to a change of 1 K, the temperature increase is 327 - 27 = 300 K (or (327 + 273.15) - (27 + 273.15) = 300 K).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: At what temperature are Celsius and Fahrenheit numerical values equal?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which statement is FALSE according to the passage?
options: Albert Sadacca invented the flat-bottomed paper bag.
Louis Braille invented a system of writing.
questions.explanation: The passage states that Margaret E. Knight invented the flat-bottomed paper bag, whereas 15-year-old Albert Sadacca invented Christmas tree lights.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which of the following happened FIRST in order of time?
options: The flat-bottomed paper bag was invented (1868)
questions.explanation: Louis Braille attended the school for blind children in 1819 and created Braille by age 15 (around 1824), before the other inventions listed.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] According to the text, why did Louis Braille want to invent a new system of writing?
options: So he could help the military write secret codes
So he could communicate with his friends more easily
So he could graduate from his school
So he could write messages in the middle of the night
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly notes: "Braille sought a better way to communicate with his classmates. He wanted to write freely, without needing special equipment."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which best describes how 11-year old Frank Epperson invented the Popsicle?
options: He tested many different formulas before finding success
He used an old family recipe, in his family for generations
He consulted with scientists and doctors to find his idea
He created it by accident when he forgot his cup of lemonade on the porch overnight
questions.explanation: The text states Frank went to bed and forgot his cup of lemonade on the porch; freezing temperatures overnight accidentally turned it into the first frozen popsicle.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which event caused 15-year old Albert Sadacca to invent safe Christmas tree lights?
options: He saw a factory worker get injured
He left his lemonade on the porch
A candle in a Christmas tree started a tragic fire
He was ice skating and his ears got cold
questions.explanation: The passage states: "Someone was hanging candles from a Christmas tree, as was common at that time. This started a tragic fire. Sadacca's parents sold electric lighting... Young Albert thought to adapt these lights for use on Christmas trees."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which statement about Chester Greenwood is FALSE?
options: He helped to employ people in his town for 60 years
His grandma helped him with his invention by sewing fur tufts to wire loops
He patented the concept of the Popsicle
He was ice skating when he had his big idea
questions.explanation: Chester Greenwood invented and patented ear protectors (earmuffs), not the Popsicle (which was invented by Frank Epperson).

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] What caused Margaret E. Knight to invent at the age of 12?
options: She left her lemonade on the porch
She wanted to better communicate with friends
A candle in a tree started a fire
She saw a loom worker get injured at a textile mill
questions.explanation: The text explains: "A loom malfunctioned and injured a worker. She thought she could make the machines safer. She invented an effective system."

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] With which statement would the author of this text most likely DISAGREE?
options: All important discoveries happen in science labs
People with disabilities have invented amazing things
Women have changed the world through invention
questions.explanation: The entire essay refutes the myth that inventions only come from "old men in white lab coats and smoky beakers," showing young children invented great things outdoors or at home.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which central lesson can readers learn from this text?
options: Age and experience are necessary to do important things
Anybody, no matter how young, can change the world
Kids should leave grown-up problems to the grown-ups
Everything important has already been invented
questions.explanation: The author states: "the truth is that everyone has the power to change the world" regardless of their young age.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: [Reading: "Child Inventors"] Which advice would the author MOST LIKELY give to young people?
options: All the problems in the world have already been solved
Children should do what they are told and not ask questions
Remain curious and think of ways to solve problems
Only adults are smart enough to change the world
questions.explanation: The author encourages youth curiosity, creative problem-solving, and confidence in making meaningful innovations.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Teacher: _________________________________________?
You: In December.
options: How do you celebrate your holiday
What do you do in your holiday
When do you celebrate your holiday
How often do you celebrate your holiday
questions.explanation: "In December" is an adverbial of time, so the appropriate question word is "When".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: We haven't done our project work _____________, but I hope we will finish it next week.
questions.explanation: "Yet" is used at the end of negative present perfect sentences to express an action expected to happen.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The medication has some nasty side effects. ____________, I started to feel quite unwell.
questions.explanation: "Therefore" is a transitional adverb expressing result/consequence connecting the side effects to feeling unwell.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
A: I am sure the views are amazing.
B: Yes, they're great. You have never been there, _____________?
questions.explanation: Because "never" gives the statement a negative meaning, the question tag must be affirmative: "have you?".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: We often go out for dinner on weekends, _____________?
questions.explanation: The main clause uses present simple with "we" ("go"), so the corresponding negative tag is "don't we?".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct adverbial order: It has been raining _____________________________.
questions.explanation: The natural royal order of adverbials in English is Manner ("heavily"), Place ("outside"), and Time ("all day long").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Teacher: Do you mind helping me once?
Student: _________________. Don't worry.
questions.explanation: When replying to "Do you mind...?", "No, I don't" means "I do not mind at all / I am glad to help".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: "He is always coming late." In communicative English, this sentence indicates:
questions.explanation: Present continuous with "always" ("is always coming late") is an idiomatic grammatical device to express irritation or annoyance with a repeated habit.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: The dogs over there are _____________ a lot of noise.
questions.explanation: In English collocation, the correct verb used with "noise" is "make" -> "making a lot of noise".

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Where is the most preferable position of the frequency adverb "often" in the sentence below?
"I (1) get headaches (2) when it is (3) very sunny (4)."
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency normally precede the main verb: "I often get headaches...". Thus position 1 is preferred.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Who _____________ the car during the accident last night?
questions.explanation: For a finished event at a specified past time ("last night"), the simple past "drove" is standard.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: He wanted to repair our washing machine that _____________ a few days before.
questions.explanation: The breaking of the machine occurred prior to the past action of wanting to repair it, requiring the past perfect "had broken".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Which sentence is incorrectly punctuated?
options: What are you doing next weekend?
The girl's father sat in a corner.
Can you tell me why I was upset?
questions.explanation: Option B is missing punctuation inside the direct speech quotation marks (it should be: '"Go away," he said!' or '"Go away!" he said.').

questions.subject: English
questions.question: "The girls want to leave now; otherwise, they might miss their favorite show." What type of adverb is "now"?
questions.explanation: "Now" answers the question "when?" and is an adverb of time.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Dawit: _____________ think of taking a break?
Nardos: I was just about to say that. Let's go.
questions.explanation: The common English phrase for asking someone's opinion on an idea is "What do you think of...?".

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Bemnet is my best friend. I _____________ him at school, and we _____________ friends for 5 years.
questions.explanation: As confirmed on the school answer key, the combination "have met / have been" indicates enduring friendship continuing into the present.

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Dawit: You look tired. You are out of breath.
Nardos: Yes, I _____________ for almost twenty minutes.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous ("have been running") emphasizes a continuous past activity with visible direct results in the present.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: I saw the accident and phoned the police _____________.
questions.explanation: "Immediately" means without any delay, fitting the urgency of calling police after witnessing an accident.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: My friend together with his sister _____________ working hard to be successful.
questions.explanation: When a subject is joined with expressions like "together with" or "as well as", the verb agrees with the principal subject ("My friend", 3rd person singular -> "is").

questions.subject: English
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate transitional sequence:
"_____________ we should consider students' academic background. _____________, it is important to know what they really need. _____________, we should look at their age level."
questions.explanation: The standard logical three-step enumerative transition sequence is "First", "Next", and "Finally".

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: A set is a collection of well-defined objects or elements.
questions.explanation: True. By mathematical definition, a set is a collection of well-defined objects such that it is clear whether any given object belongs to the set or not.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: A set which does not contain any element is called a void (or empty) set.
questions.explanation: True. A set with no elements is called a void, null, or empty set, denoted by ∅ or {}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: A set which consists of a definite (countable) number of elements is called a finite set.
questions.explanation: True. If the elements of a set can be counted and the counting process terminates at a natural number n, the set is finite.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: Two sets A and B are said to be equal if and only if they have exactly the same or identical elements.
questions.explanation: True. By the axiom of extensionality, A = B if and only if every element of A is in B and every element of B is in A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: If A ⊆ B and A ≠ B, then A is called the proper subset of set B.
questions.explanation: True. A proper subset A ⊂ B means A is contained in B but B has at least one element not present in A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: Two sets A and B are disjoint if A ∩ B = ∅.
questions.explanation: True. Disjoint sets share no common elements, meaning their intersection is the empty set.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: A fraction a/b is said to be in simplest (lowest) form if a and b are relatively prime or GCF(a, b) = 1.
questions.explanation: True. When the greatest common factor of the numerator and denominator is 1, the fraction cannot be simplified further.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: Every natural number can be expressed as a product of primes and this factorization is unique.
questions.explanation: False. The number 1 is a natural number but has no prime factors (the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic applies to integers greater than 1).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: If a is a rational number and b is an irrational number, then ab is always a rational number.
questions.explanation: False. For example, 2 × √3 = 2√3 which is irrational (the only exception where ab is rational is when a = 0).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: For two positive integers a and b in the division lemma (a = bq + r), we say a is divisible by b if the remainder r is zero.
questions.explanation: True. If remainder r = 0, then a = bq, meaning b divides a completely without remainder.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: True or False: If a is a natural number then it is either prime or composite.
questions.explanation: False. 1 is a natural number, but 1 is neither prime nor composite.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Given universal set U = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9}, A = {2, 5, 7, 9}, and B = {2, 3, 5, 7, 8}. Find A' ∩ B'.
questions.explanation: By De Morgan's Law, A' ∩ B' = (A ∪ B)'. Here A ∪ B = {2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9}. Its complement in U is {1, 4, 6}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Find GCF(12, 18) × LCM(12, 18).
questions.explanation: For any two positive numbers, GCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b. Therefore, 12 × 18 = 216.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: In a bookstore there are 125 different books to be distributed to 9 students. If the store shares these books equally, how many books will each student receive and how many books will be left?
questions.explanation: 125 ÷ 9 = 13 with remainder 8. Each student receives 13 books, and 8 books are left over.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question:
Which of the following are well-defined sets?
A: Collection of students in your class
B: Collection of beautiful girls in your class
C: Collection of consonants of the English alphabet
D: The collection of kind students in your school
questions.explanation: Sets A and C have objective criteria ("students registered in class", "letters other than vowels"). Words like "beautiful" or "kind" are subjective opinions and not well-defined.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Suppose that A is the set of positive even numbers. Which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, ...}. 4 is a positive even number, so 4 ∈ A. -2 is negative, 0 is neither positive nor negative, and 5 is odd.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following is an infinite set?
options: C is the set of odd natural numbers divisible by 2
questions.explanation: Between any two real numbers 5 and 6, there are infinitely many real numbers. B has 1 element, C is empty (0 elements), and D is empty.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Any set is a subset of itself
Empty set is a subset of every set
For any set A, A is not a proper subset of itself
The number of proper subsets of set A with n elements is 2n - 1
questions.explanation: The formula for the number of proper subsets is 2ⁿ - 1 (exponential), not 2n - 1.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Which of the following set identities is false?
questions.explanation: ∅ ∪ A = A (the union of any set with the empty set is the set itself, not ∅).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For any two sets A and B, which of the following is false?
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference is defined as A Δ B = (A \ B) ∪ (B \ A), with a UNION, not intersection (their intersection is always ∅).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Given A = {0, 2, 3, 4, 5} and B = {0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Find the symmetric difference A Δ B.
questions.explanation: A \ B = {4}, B \ A = {1, 7, 9}. Their union is A Δ B = {1, 4, 7, 9}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: If the number of elements of set A is 7 and the number of elements of set B is 4, then the number of elements in Cartesian product A × B is:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: For any two sets A and B, which of the following is false?
options: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B)
n(A Δ B) = n(A) + n(B) - 2n(A ∩ B)
questions.explanation: The correct identity is n(A \ B) = n(A) - n(A ∩ B), not n(A) - n(B).

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Consider universal set U = {1, 2, 3 ... 14}, A = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11}, and B = {2, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11}. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: A \ B removes elements of B ({2, 11}) from A, leaving exactly {3, 5, 7}.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of 180, 270, and 1,080 using prime factorization.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question: Given that 77,9x2 is a 5-digit number where x is the tens digit. If this number is divisible by 6, what are all possible values of x?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 6, the number must be even (last digit 2 is even) and divisible by 3. Sum of digits: 7 + 7 + 9 + x + 2 = 25 + x. For (25 + x) to be divisible by 3, x can be 2 (27), 5 (30), or 8 (33).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: True or False: Dichotomous keys are useful for taxonomists to classify unfamiliar organisms.
questions.explanation: True. A dichotomous key presents paired alternative statements to guide the step-by-step identification of organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: True or False: Biology is related to chemistry and physics during studying the process of photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: True. Photosynthesis involves light energy absorption (physics) and chemical reactions converting CO2 and water into glucose (chemistry).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: True or False: The correct way of handling/carrying a microscope is holding it with one hand only.
questions.explanation: False. A microscope must always be carried with two hands: one grasping the arm and the other supporting the base.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: True or False: It is permissible to taste and sniff chemicals in laboratory rooms.
questions.explanation: False. In laboratory safety, tasting chemicals is strictly forbidden, and smelling should only be done cautiously by wafting.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: True or False: In symbiotic association between fungi and termites, fungi supply extracellular hydrolytic enzymes to break down cellulose.
questions.explanation: True. Termites cultivate fungus combs, and fungal cellulase enzymes break down indigestible plant cellulose for termite nutrition.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which part of the optical microscope is used to move the mechanical stage rapidly for initial focusing?
questions.explanation: The coarse adjustment knob moves the stage in large increments to bring the specimen quickly into approximate focus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which part of the microscope moves the stage slowly to produce a sharp, crisp focus?
questions.explanation: The fine adjustment knob provides precision micro-movements of the stage to achieve exact optical clarity.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which component of a microscope controls the intensity and amount of light reaching the specimen?
questions.explanation: The iris diaphragm regulates the diameter of the light cone passing through the specimen slide.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which microscope part collects and focuses light rays from the illuminator onto the specimen?
questions.explanation: The sub-stage condenser lens concentrates and focuses the light beam onto the slide plane.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which apparatus is used in laboratories to provide high-pressure steam for complete sterilization?
questions.explanation: An autoclave uses pressurized saturated steam at 121 °C to kill all microbial life and bacterial endospores.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The ancient Greek philosopher who divided animals into two groups (those with red blood and those without) was:
questions.explanation: Aristotle created the earliest classical animal taxonomy, classifying animals into Enaima (with red blood) and Anaima (without red blood).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The criteria used in R.H. Whittaker's five-kingdom classification system include:
questions.explanation: Whittaker (1969) built the five kingdoms (Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) using cellular complexity, nutrition mode, and evolutionary relationships.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following biological groups are included within Whittaker's five kingdoms?
questions.explanation: Bacteria belong to Kingdom Monera, and unicellular/multicellular algae belong to Protista and Plantae. Viruses and lichens are excluded from Whittaker's kingdoms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The naturalist who developed binomial nomenclature and authored "Systema Naturae" is:
questions.explanation: Carolus Linnaeus established formal binomial nomenclature (Genus + specific epithet) in his 1735 book "Systema Naturae".

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What primary method of asexual reproduction is used by yeast?
questions.explanation: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (yeast) reproduces asexually through asymmetrical budding, where a new daughter cell pinches off from the parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Protists are ecologically vital because they:
options: Support marine and freshwater food chains
Recycle organic nutrients in aquatic habitats
questions.explanation: Protists carry out immense oceanic primary productivity, oxygen generation, nutrient cycling, and sustain aquatic food webs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungi are indispensable to global ecosystems primarily because they function as:
questions.explanation: Fungi secrete exoenzymes that decompose complex organic detritus (cellulose and lignin), recycling mineral nutrients back to soil.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which statement is true regarding a well-designed controlled experiment?
options: Isolates one independent variable while measuring a dependent variable
Keeps all other environmental variables strictly controlled
questions.explanation: A scientific controlled experiment maintains constant experimental parameters to isolate the exact effect of the independent variable on the dependent variable.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-hyphal (unicellular) fungus?
questions.explanation: Yeast is uniquely unicellular and does not produce true multicellular filamentous hyphae like molds (Mucor, Rhizopus) or mushrooms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cellular structures are used as locomotive appendages in unicellular organisms?
questions.explanation: Euglena moves by flagella, Paramecium uses cilia, and Amoeba moves using amoeboid cytoplasmic extensions called pseudopodia.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following protists is free-living and does NOT cause human infectious disease?
questions.explanation: Paramecium is a harmless, free-living ciliated pond protist. Plasmodium causes malaria, Giardia causes giardiasis, and Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which method of asexual reproduction is characteristic of Paramecium?
questions.explanation: Paramecium divides asexually via transverse binary fission, producing two identical daughter ciliate cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a difference between fungi and animals?
options: Fungi have chitinous cell walls whereas animals lack cell walls
Fungi are heterotrophs while animals are autotrophs
Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs while animals are ingestive heterotrophs
Fungi are non-motile while animals are motile
questions.explanation: Both fungi and animals are heterotrophs (neither are autotrophs). Stating animals are not heterotrophic is false.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungi resemble animals because they are:
questions.explanation: Fungi share phylogenetic kinship with animals as heterotrophs that store carbohydrates as glycogen rather than starch.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: All of the following are asexual modes of reproduction in fungi EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Conjugation is a sexual process involving nuclear exchange and genetic recombination, whereas budding, sporulation, and fragmentation are asexual.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The vegetative body of multicellular fungi (mycelium) is composed of microscopic tubular branched filaments called:
questions.explanation: Hyphae are the thread-like fungal filaments that weave together to constitute the fungal mycelium.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Protozoan protists are traditionally classified into classes primarily according to:
options: Their mechanism of locomotion (cilia, flagella, pseudopodia)
questions.explanation: Protozoa are systematically grouped by their mode of movement: flagellates, ciliates, amoeboids (pseudopodia), and non-motile sporozoans.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following Archaebacteria can thrive in aerobic, hypersaline environments?
questions.explanation: Extremely halophilic Archaea (Halophiles) live in extreme salt lakes and require high NaCl concentrations, carrying out aerobic respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During binary fission, which statement accurately describes the resulting daughter cells?
options: They have half as many chromosomes as the parent cell
They have double the chromosome number
They have the same chromosome count as the parent but initial smaller cell volume
questions.explanation: Binary fission produces two genetically identical daughter cells with the exact full parental complement of chromosomes, which then grow in size.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches the organism with its cell wall chemical composition?
options: All of the above are correct
questions.explanation: All three pairings accurately depict the respective cell wall biochemical constituents.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: Feresula is a traditional unit to measure time.
questions.explanation: False. In Ethiopian traditional measurement, the "Feresula" is an indigenous unit of mass (equal to approximately 17 kg), not time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: The number 1.020 has four significant figures.
questions.explanation: True. The '1' and '2' are non-zero, the zero between them is captive, and the trailing zero after the decimal point is significant, totaling 4 significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: The number 1,000,000 is denoted by the metric prefix mega.
questions.explanation: True. The SI prefix "mega" (M) denotes a multiplier factor of 10⁶ = 1,000,000.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.
questions.explanation: True. By standard significant figure rules, captive zeros (zeros between two non-zero digits) are always significant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: Leading zeros are significant if the number has a decimal point.
questions.explanation: False. Leading zeros (such as the zeros in 0.005) merely show the position of the decimal point and are never significant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: True or False: In addition, the rules for significant figures are the same as in division.
questions.explanation: False. In addition/subtraction, precision is determined by the fewest decimal places; in multiplication/division, precision is determined by the fewest significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental physical quantity?
questions.explanation: Time (measured in seconds) is one of the seven SI fundamental/base physical quantities. Area, volume, and density are derived.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When adding or subtracting significant figures, the result should have the same number with:
questions.explanation: The result of addition or subtraction must be rounded to match the value with the fewest decimal places (least decimal precision).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The prefix "Nano" represents:
questions.explanation: The metric prefix nano- corresponds to 10⁻⁹. Micro- is 10⁻⁶ and giga- is 10⁹.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which one of the following innovations was contributed by Sir Isaac Newton?
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton made foundational discoveries in universal gravitation, classical mechanics (laws of motion), calculus, and optics (prism dispersion).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which one of the following numbers has the greatest number of significant figures?
questions.explanation: 0.020 has 2 significant figures (the '2' and trailing '0'). 2000 has 1, 0.001 has 1, and 50000 has 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The number 25.373 rounded to 3 significant figures is:
questions.explanation: The first three significant figures are 2, 5, and 3. The following digit is 7 (≥ 5), so 3 rounds up to 4, giving 25.4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Multiply 500 × 2.4 and report with the correct number of significant figures:
questions.explanation: 500 has 1 significant figure, and 2.4 has 2. 500 × 2.4 = 1200, which rounds to 1 significant figure as 1000.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Subtract 35.25 - 34 and report with the correct number of significant figures:
questions.explanation: 35.25 has 2 decimal places and 34 has 0 decimal places. 35.25 - 34 = 1.25, rounded to 0 decimal places gives 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT equivalent to 1 hour?
questions.explanation: 0.24 day equals 0.24 × 24 = 5.76 hours, which is not equivalent to 1 hour.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One metric ton is equivalent to which of the following?
questions.explanation: 1 metric ton = 1,000 kg = 10 quintals (1 quintal = 100 kg) = 1,000,000 grams. All expressions are equivalent.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which physicist explained the photoelectric effect in 1905, establishing light quanta?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his theoretical explanation of the photoelectric effect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientist experimentally determined the mechanical equivalent of heat?
questions.explanation: James Prescott Joule showed the equivalence of mechanical work and thermal energy, giving his name to the SI unit of energy (Joule).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which pioneering scientist discovered radium and polonium, winning two Nobel Prizes?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie discovered the radioactive elements radium and polonium.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which scientist discovered electromagnetic induction and formulated laws governing magnetic flux and induced EMF?
questions.explanation: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which branch of physics deals with the study of motion and forces?
questions.explanation: Mechanics is the foundation branch of physics studying motion, forces, momentum, and energy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which branch of physics studies the behavior of heat, work, and temperature?
questions.explanation: Thermodynamics governs heat transfer, thermodynamic laws, work, and entropy.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which branch of physics deals with electric and magnetic fields and their interactions?
questions.explanation: Electromagnetism encompasses electrostatics, magnetostatics, circuits, and electromagnetic waves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which branch of physics is concerned with the generation, propagation, and detection of sound waves?
questions.explanation: Acoustics is the physical study of mechanical sound and vibration waves in various media.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which branch of physics studies the behavior, properties, and transmission of light?
questions.explanation: Optics studies reflection, refraction, lenses, diffraction, and properties of light.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How many significant figures are in the measurement 30.250 m?
questions.explanation: 30.250 has five significant figures (the '3', captive '0', '2', '5', and trailing '0' in decimal).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: True or False: Prehistory refers to the period after the invention of writing.
questions.explanation: False. Prehistory specifically refers to the period before writing was invented. The period after the invention of writing is recorded history.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: True or False: The Greek word Istoria means "inquiry" or "an account of one's inquiries."
questions.explanation: True. The English word history originates from the ancient Greek word "istoria" (inquiry, knowledge acquired by investigation).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: True or False: One of the key aims of history is to help us understand the present.
questions.explanation: True. Studying past events, trends, and cause-effect relationships provides essential context for understanding contemporary societies and institutions.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: True or False: Oral sources never need to be verified because they are always accurate.
questions.explanation: False. Oral traditions can be distorted by human memory, bias, and selective transmission over generations; historians must rigorously cross-check and verify oral sources.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: True or False: In Ethiopian historiography, history became an academic discipline in the 1960s.
questions.explanation: True. Professional academic historiography in Ethiopia was established in the 1960s with the foundation of the Department of History and Institute of Ethiopian Studies at Haile Selassie I University (now Addis Ababa University).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which hominid species is known as "The upright man"?
questions.explanation: Homo erectus literally translates to "upright man" because it was the first hominid known to walk fully upright and migrate out of Africa.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which species is classified as "The wise man" and encompasses all modern humans?
questions.explanation: Homo sapiens translates from Latin as "wise man" or "knowing man".

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following historical items serves as a primary archaeological source?
questions.explanation: Monuments, coins, inscriptions, and fossils are physical primary sources created during the time period under study.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a secondary source of history?
questions.explanation: History books are secondary sources because they analyze, synthesize, and interpret primary sources after the events took place.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which early human ancestor is known as "The handy man" due to its use of stone tools?
questions.explanation: Homo habilis was named "the handy man" by Louis Leakey because fossils were found directly alongside Oldowan stone tools.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary source of history?
questions.explanation: A history textbook is written by researchers who compile and analyze primary sources, making it a secondary source.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which area of human life is not a direct concern of early history?
questions.explanation: Early human survival and social organisation focused on food gathering/production, shelter, and political organization; individual music preferences are not a direct concern of early history.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary source of history?
options: A newspaper article from 2020 about World War II.
A letter written during World War I.
questions.explanation: A letter written during World War I is a direct firsthand primary source from someone living through the event.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: All modern humans belong to the species of _______
questions.explanation: All modern humans belong strictly to the species Homo sapiens.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The term history comes from the Greek word Istoria, which means _______
questions.explanation: The ancient Greek term "istoria" means inquiry, investigation, or learning through inquiry.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Thucydides is best known for _______
options: Promoting factual and critical historical writing.
questions.explanation: The Greek historian Thucydides is celebrated for applying rigorous critical standards, factual evidence, and rejecting supernatural causes in his History of the Peloponnesian War.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Before using historical sources, historians must _______
questions.explanation: Historical methodology requires internal and external criticism to evaluate the authenticity and reliability of sources.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is a major aim of studying history?
options: To understand the present and plan for the future.
questions.explanation: History aims to illuminate how past decisions shaped modern conditions so societies can plan wisely for the future.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: In the Paleolithic Age, people primarily practice _______
questions.explanation: During the Paleolithic (Old Stone Age), humans lived in nomadic bands relying on hunting game and foraging/gathering wild edible plants.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following is the term for identifying when a historical event happened?
questions.explanation: Dating (both relative dating and absolute scientific dating like Carbon-14) determines chronological time in history and archaeology.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: What does prehistory refer to?
options: The study of space and time.
The time before writing was invented.
questions.explanation: Prehistory encompasses all of human existence prior to the invention of written documentation.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Neolithic developments in Ethiopia included _______
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian region is recognized as a major Vavilov centre of plant domestication, cultivating indigenous crops like teff, enset, and coffee during the Neolithic era.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who is known as the Father of History?
questions.explanation: Herodotus of Halicarnassus was first titled "The Father of History" by Cicero for his systematic collection and inquiry of the Greco-Persian wars.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Leopold Von Ranke is famous for:
options: Introducing scientific methods to historical writing.
questions.explanation: Ranke transformed modern history into a scientific discipline focused on primary archival documents and objective depiction of "wie es eigentlich gewesen" (how it actually happened).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: A period of 1,000 years is known as _______
questions.explanation: A millennium represents 1,000 years (a decade is 10 years, a century is 100 years).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Islamic calendar starts counting time from _______
questions.explanation: The Hijri calendar begins in 622 CE when Prophet Muhammad migrated from Mecca to Medina (the Hijrah).

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The famous fossil "Lucy" belongs to the species of _______
questions.explanation: Lucy (Dinkinesh), unearthed in Hadar (Afar, Ethiopia) by Donald Johanson in 1974, is an Australopithecus afarensis dated to ~3.2 million years ago.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The Neolithic Revolution refers to _______
options: The shift from hunting to farming.
questions.explanation: The Neolithic Revolution was the monumental transition of human societies from mobile hunting and gathering to settled agriculture and animal husbandry.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: The tool inventions like the hoe and wheel belong to the:
questions.explanation: Ground stone axes, hoes for tilling soil, pottery, and wheeled carts emerged during the Neolithic revolution.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: According to the agricultural theory, the state developed as a result of:
questions.explanation: Agricultural food surplus enabled population growth, occupational specialization, trade, social stratification, and centralized administrative state structures.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: Ethics is the same as morality, and the terms can be used interchangeably.
questions.explanation: False. While related, morality generally refers to personal or cultural beliefs about right and wrong, whereas ethics is the systematic, philosophical study and principles governing conduct.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: A person with integrity always aligns their actions with their words.
questions.explanation: True. Integrity means honesty, consistency, and having high moral principles where actions faithfully correspond to verbal commitments.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: Ethics only deals with personal feelings and opinions, not real-life actions.
questions.explanation: False. Ethics is profoundly concerned with real-life actions, human relationships, societal rules, and institutional behavior.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: One of the key values of ethics is disobedience to the law when it feels inconvenient.
questions.explanation: False. Respect for the rule of law and civic responsibility are core values of citizenship and ethics.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: Respect means treating others with dignity, regardless of differences in background.
questions.explanation: True. Mutual respect recognizes the universal dignity and human rights of all individuals without discrimination.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: Concern for others excludes people with disabilities, as they require separate laws.
questions.explanation: False. Inclusive citizenship emphasizes compassion, equal opportunities, protection, and concern for persons with disabilities.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: True or False: Promise-keeping is a part of integrity that strengthens trust and relationships.
questions.explanation: True. Honoring promises and commitments establishes credibility and creates social trust.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Match: Which ethical value describes "Being honest, reliable, and morally upright"?
questions.explanation: Integrity denotes wholeness of moral character, truthfulness, and upholding ethical standards.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Match: Which civic duty involves "Following rules and upholding justice"?
questions.explanation: Obeying the law means adhering to established legal frameworks and respecting constitutional order.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Match: Which term corresponds to "Being honest and dependable in relationships"?
questions.explanation: Trustworthiness is the quality of inspiring confidence through honesty, dependability, and faithfulness.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Match: Which term is defined as "Being faithful to individuals, society, and country"?
questions.explanation: Loyalty involves unswerving allegiance, duty, and faithfulness to community and country.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Match: Which quality entails "Striving for quality and constant self-improvement"?
questions.explanation: Commitment to excellence means striving to achieve the highest possible standard in studies, work, and personal growth.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: A society with ethical citizens is characterized by _______
options: Sustainable peace, unity, and rule of law.
questions.explanation: Ethical citizenship fosters rule of law, mutual harmony, social trust, and lasting peace.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Theoretical ethics is mainly concerned with _______
options: The origin and nature of moral judgments.
questions.explanation: Meta-ethics / theoretical ethics explores fundamental philosophical questions regarding the origins, nature, and meaning of moral values.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Commitment to excellence requires to _______
questions.explanation: Excellence requires diligent hard work, dedication, resilience, and steady personal development.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: What we learn from Ethics?
options: Act in morally sound ways and avoid unethical actions.
questions.explanation: Ethics guides moral behavior, encouraging good conduct and prevention of harmful or corrupt actions.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: What does it mean respect for humanity?
options: Supporting only people of similar background.
Treating all people equally regardless of differences.
questions.explanation: Respect for humanity requires honoring the universal dignity of all persons regardless of ethnicity, religion, or social class.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: The term ethics originates from the Greek word ethos, which means:
questions.explanation: The word ethics derives from the ancient Greek "ethos", meaning custom, disposition, habit, or character.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Being free from addiction is considered an attribute of _______
questions.explanation: Maintaining physical, mental, and moral self-control and freedom from destructive addictions reflects personal integrity and responsible self-care.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Ethical values serve as:
options: Guiding principles to distinguish right from wrong.
questions.explanation: Ethical values act as moral compasses that guide human choices, distinguishing right from wrong.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Which of the following is not listed as a key ethical value?
questions.explanation: Laziness is a vice and negative habit, not an ethical value.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: What is the meaning of Integrity?
options: Staying true to moral principles in both private and public life.
Seeking personal success at any cost.
questions.explanation: Integrity is the practice of consistently adhering to ethical and moral principles, whether in public scrutiny or in private.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Ethics mainly deals with:
options: Moral principles and values guiding human behavior.
questions.explanation: Ethics is the branch of philosophy concerning moral guidelines and rules governing human conduct.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: A person with integrity is characterized by:
questions.explanation: Honesty, consistency, dependability, and ethical steadfastness are hallmarks of integrity.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Ethical values are essential for citizens. Why? B/c
options: Build a peaceful, just, and harmonious society.
questions.explanation: Ethical citizens create the bedrock of justice, security, mutual trust, and national solidarity.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Practical ethics focuses on:
options: Applying moral principles in real-life situations.
questions.explanation: Applied (practical) ethics examines how moral theory is applied to real-world dilemmas in medicine, business, environment, and social life.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Abiding by the law ensures:
questions.explanation: Lawfulness guarantees public safety, social order, equality before the law, and civil protection.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Without ethical guidelines, society would _______
questions.explanation: Without moral boundaries, lawlessness, exploitation, and social breakdown make civilized life impossible.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Ethics is important in daily life because it helps us:
options: Decide what is acceptable and unacceptable behavior.
questions.explanation: Ethics helps individuals make responsible daily choices between right and wrong.

questions.subject: Citizenship
questions.question: Promise-keeping as an ethical value strengthens:
questions.explanation: Fulfilling commitments creates mutual dependability and bonds of social trust.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: Microeconomics deals with individual consumers and firms.
questions.explanation: True. Microeconomics examines the economic decision-making of individual agents such as single consumers, households, and business firms.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: Normative economics is value-free and objective.
questions.explanation: False. Positive economics is factual and value-free. Normative economics deals with what "ought to be" and is based on subjective value judgments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: Households are the buyers of factors of production.
questions.explanation: False. In the circular flow of income, households own and sell factors of production (land, labor, capital) while business firms are the buyers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: In a command economy, all production is controlled by private firms.
questions.explanation: False. In a command (socialist) economy, economic decisions and production are controlled by the central government, not private firms.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: Capitalism allows private ownership and competition.
questions.explanation: True. A capitalist market economy is based on private ownership of property, freedom of enterprise, and competitive markets.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: True or False: Deductive and inductive methods compete with each other.
questions.explanation: False. Deductive and inductive methods are complementary approaches in economic analysis, often used together to form and test theories.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The basic economic problem arises because:
options: Resources are scarce but wants are unlimited
questions.explanation: Scarcity is the fundamental economic problem: society has limited productive resources to satisfy unlimited human needs and desires.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Opportunity cost refers to:
questions.explanation: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative that is given up when a choice is made.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which point on a PPF (Production Possibility Frontier) is unattainable?
questions.explanation: Points outside the PPF curve represent combinations that cannot be produced with the current resources and technology.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: "How to produce goods?" is also called:
questions.explanation: "How to produce?" deals with choosing the method or technique of production, such as labor-intensive versus capital-intensive techniques.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which is a characteristic of a mixed economy?
options: Co-existence of private and public sectors
questions.explanation: A mixed economic system combines elements of private enterprise with public government intervention.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: The deductive method proceeds from:
questions.explanation: Deductive reasoning moves from general principles and assumptions to specific logical conclusions.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of normative economics?
questions.explanation: Normative statements express opinions and value judgments regarding what policies ought to be implemented.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Among the following, which one is a scarce resource?
questions.explanation: Land is an economic resource with a limited supply and positive price, unlike ambient air or sunlight.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following is correct?
options: Any disagreement on normative economics can be resolved through fact
Economic growth can be one concern of microeconomics
Inductive reasoning analyze from specific to general
questions.explanation: Inductive reasoning begins with specific empirical observations and facts to formulate general principles.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which of the following statements would best describe firms?
options: They are owners of factor resources
They mix factor resources and change it into one final output
They are buyers of final output
questions.explanation: Firms combine factors of production (labor, raw materials, capital) to produce finished goods and services.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Given a country's production combinations: Combination C (20 Machines, 100 Food) and Combination D (30 Machines, 0 Food). What is the total opportunity cost in food when moving from C to D to produce 10 extra machines?
questions.explanation: Moving from C (100 food) to D (0 food) requires giving up 100 - 0 = 100 units of food.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When moving from combination C (20 Machines, 100 Food) to D (30 Machines, 0 Food), what is the per-unit opportunity cost of producing each additional machine?
questions.explanation: Per-unit opportunity cost = Sacrificed Food / Gained Machines = (100 - 0) / (30 - 20) = 100 / 10 = 10 units of food per machine.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: Save allows you to update a previously saved file with new content.
questions.explanation: True. The Save command writes updates and modifications directly to the existing file path without prompting for a new filename.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: Renaming a file does not remove its content.
questions.explanation: True. Renaming simply modifies the file identifier in the directory index while the data bytes remain intact.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: Windows does not allow handling multiple files.
questions.explanation: False. Operating systems like Windows support multi-file selection (using Ctrl/Shift), batch renaming, moving, and deleting.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: A folder is also called a directory.
questions.explanation: True. Directory is the file system term, while folder is the graphical user interface term; both represent storage containers.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: A storage drive can be fixed and removable.
questions.explanation: True. Internal hard disk/SSD drives are fixed, while USB flash drives and external hard drives are removable.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: Each file in a computer has unique icons.
questions.explanation: False. Files sharing the same file extension (.docx, .pdf, .txt) share the same default application icon.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: Software cannot be shared over the network.
questions.explanation: False. Software, web applications, and network licenses are routinely shared and accessed across local networks and the internet.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: True or False: MAN covers the area of a city and can contain multiple WANs.
questions.explanation: False. A Wide Area Network (WAN) spans countries and continents; a Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) covers a city and cannot contain WANs.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which type of icon can take you to another place or open a file quickly?
questions.explanation: A shortcut icon (indicated by a small arrow) links directly to a file, folder, or application elsewhere on the drive.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: _______ displays information about a selected folder and its contents.
questions.explanation: The Status Bar at the bottom of the window displays item count, selected count, and size information.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: _______ is used to enable you to perform layout, formatting and sharing tasks.
questions.explanation: The Ribbon toolbar organizes tools into tabs (Home, Insert, Layout) for editing, formatting, and operations.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: _______ means locating a file among a set of files.
questions.explanation: Searching allows the user to find files by typing their name, extension, or keywords in the search bar.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which one of the following is not used to move files?
questions.explanation: Cut and paste, Drag-and-drop, and the "Move to" menu command are all standard techniques to move files.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: In a computer, a file can be _______
questions.explanation: Computer files store documents, executable programs, video, audio, images, and other digital data.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which one of the following devices is used to select the appropriate path within a network?
questions.explanation: A Router inspects destination IP addresses and determines the optimal routing path between different network segments.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: The network system that spans states, countries or the whole world is _______
questions.explanation: A Wide Area Network (WAN) connects computers over large geographical areas such as countries and continents.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: A network system within a single building or school campus is _______
questions.explanation: A Local Area Network (LAN) covers a small geographic area such as an office, home, or school campus.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which device accepts a weak signal, then boosts it to its original strength and forwards it to the next network segment?
questions.explanation: A Repeater amplifies and regenerates attenuated signals to extend network transmission distances.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which one of the following is an optical disk drive?
questions.explanation: Both CD and DVD drives use laser optics to read and write data on circular discs.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: _______ is a hardware storage unit of a computer which stores files and folders.
questions.explanation: A storage Drive (such as C: drive, SSD, HDD) holds files, folders, and operating system data.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which one of the following is not an image editing software?
questions.explanation: Paint, GIMP, and Photoshop are all widely recognized bitmap/raster image editing programs.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Which one of the following is found under Quick Access in File Explorer?
questions.explanation: Quick Access pins frequently accessed folders including Desktop, Documents, Downloads, and Pictures.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: A short-range wireless network created by Bluetooth is known as _______
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) covers personal devices within a short radius (~10 meters), commonly using Bluetooth.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Suppose a bank wants to connect three of its branches in a given city, which type of network solves the problem?
questions.explanation: A Metropolitan Area Network (MAN) is designed to connect facilities and branch offices across an entire city.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: Which component is described as "Used to manage files and folders"?
questions.explanation: File Explorer (formerly Windows Explorer) provides the graphical user interface for managing files and folders.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: In a network architecture, a workstation or personal computer acts as an:
questions.explanation: End devices (hosts, PCs, smartphones) form the source and destination of data messages across a network.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: What interface area lets you "View your computer's file and folder structure"?
questions.explanation: The Navigation pane on the left side of File Explorer shows the hierarchical folder tree and drives.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: A Network Interface Card (NIC) is classified as an:
questions.explanation: The NIC provides physical connectivity and network interface intermediation.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: What is defined as a "Collection of data or information stored under a name"?
questions.explanation: A file is a named collection of related data stored on computer storage.

questions.subject: IT
questions.question: Match: What represents a "Set of rules to guide communications across a network"?
questions.explanation: Protocols (such as TCP/IP, HTTP) define standard rules and formats for exchanging data over networks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: Which prominent mountain peak belongs to The Plateau of Tigray?
questions.explanation: Mount Ambalage is located in the northern plateau of Tigray.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: Which highest Ethiopian mountain is situated in The North Central Massif?
questions.explanation: Mount Ras Dashen (4,550m in the Simien Mountains) belongs to the North Central Massifs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: Which peak is located on The Plateau of Shewa?
questions.explanation: Mount Abbuye Meda (4,012m) is situated in the Shewan plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: Which highlands are located in The Southwestern Highlands of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The Gamo-Konso highlands form part of the rugged southwestern Ethiopian highlands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: The Mesozoic geological era is characterized biologically by:
questions.explanation: The Mesozoic era (Age of Reptiles) was dominated by reptiles and dinosaurs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Match: The Paleozoic geological era is characterized biologically by:
questions.explanation: The Paleozoic era witnessed the explosion and predominance of marine invertebrates, fish, and early amphibians.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following elements of geographical study is related to Demography?
questions.explanation: Demography is the scientific statistical study of human populations, including births, deaths, growth, and migration.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which sub-division of the lowlands of Ethiopia is found in the northwestern part of the country?
questions.explanation: The Tekeze and Angereb lowlands border northwestern Ethiopia and Sudan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which physiographic division of Ethiopia is highly affected by volcanic eruptions and earthquakes?
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian Rift Valley is a tectonically active fault zone marked by geothermal activity, active volcanoes, and seismic tremors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: _______ and _______ are the highest and lowest places in Ethiopia respectively.
questions.explanation: Ras Dashen is Ethiopia's highest point (4,550 m above sea level), and the Dallol depression in Afar is the lowest (-125 m below sea level).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one of the following combinations of mountains and highlands of Ethiopia is NOT CORRECT?
options: Gara muleta -> The Plateau of Tigray
Abbuye Meda -> The Plateau of Shewa
questions.explanation: Gara Muleta is located in the Hararghe (Eastern) Highlands, not the Tigray Plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which plateau serves as a watershed between the Awash and Abay river basins?
questions.explanation: The Shewan plateau forms the drainage divide separating the westward-flowing Abay (Blue Nile) from the rift-ward Awash basin.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The Great East African Rift Valley extends from _______ to _______
questions.explanation: The system extends approximately 6,000 kilometers from the Jordan Valley and Syria in the north down to Mozambique in southeastern Africa.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Geologically, which area is the most unstable part of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: The Rift Valley floor sits directly above crustal spreading centres, making it the most tectonically unstable region in Ethiopia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which part of the Geosphere is termed as the rock (solid) layer of the earth?
questions.explanation: The lithosphere is the solid, rocky outer layer of the Earth consisting of the crust and uppermost mantle.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Dinosaurs disappeared from the earth during the:
questions.explanation: Dinosaurs went extinct at the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction boundary at the end of the Mesozoic era (~66 million years ago).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Series trapping lava and extensive volcanic eruptions were common in Ethiopia during the:
questions.explanation: During the Cenozoic era, massive flood basalt volcanism poured out the Trappean series forming the highland plateaus.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following is not an endogenic (internal) force?
questions.explanation: Erosion is an exogenic (external weathering/denudation) process driven by water, wind, and gravity.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Upper sandstone of Ethiopia was deposited during the _______ period.
questions.explanation: During the Cretaceous marine regression, the Upper Sandstone formation was deposited.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The extreme point that lies at the westernmost tip of Ethiopia is:
questions.explanation: Akobo in the Gambella region is Ethiopia's westernmost geographical extreme point.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which neighboring country shares the longest boundary line with Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Somalia shares the longest international land border with Ethiopia (~1,600 km).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The most overlying Mesozoic rock layer in Ethiopia is:
questions.explanation: In the Mesozoic stratigraphic column of Ethiopia, Upper Sandstone sits at the top, deposited as the Mesozoic sea retreated.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Among the following fields of physical geography, which one studies the forces that change land forms?
questions.explanation: Geomorphology is the study of the physical features of the Earth's surface and their relation to its geological structures and forces.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The present land forms of Ethiopia mainly resulted from the geologic events of:
questions.explanation: Tertiary uplift, faulting, rifting, and Quaternary deposition created modern Ethiopian relief and topography.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which areas of the following highlands of Ethiopia are the wettest?
questions.explanation: The Southwestern highlands (around Kaffa and Illubabor) receive the highest annual rainfall in Ethiopia (over 2,200 mm).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: What makes Ethiopia "the roof of North-Eastern" Africa?
options: Its large proportion of Arable land
questions.explanation: Over 50% of all African land above 2,000 meters elevation is found in Ethiopia, earning it the title "the roof of Northeast Africa".

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: As Adigrat sandstone is to Triassic period, then Hintalo limestone is to:
questions.explanation: Adigrat sandstone was deposited during the Triassic transgression, followed by Hintalo limestone during maximum Jurassic inundation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which geological era is known as an era of amphibians?
questions.explanation: The late Paleozoic era (Carboniferous period) is renowned as the Age of Amphibians.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: One can associate the Cenozoic era in Ethiopia with the formation of extensive:
questions.explanation: Massive Cenozoic volcanic trap series produced vast basaltic and rhyolitic igneous formations.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The plateau of Tigray is separated from the plateaus of Eritrea by the:
questions.explanation: The Mereb (Gash) River forms the natural boundary separating the Tigray Plateau from the Eritrean highlands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the Great East African Rift Valley?
options: It extends from Syria to Mozambique.
It is formed as a result of folding.
It is the second largest in the world.
All Ethiopia lakes are found in the rift-Valley.
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley system extends across ~6,000 km from Syria to Mozambique.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Nutrition is a chemical substance in our food.
questions.explanation: True. Nutrients are chemical compounds in food that provide energy, structural materials, and regulating agents.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Health is an optimal state of health and wellbeing.
