questions.explanation: False. Health is defined by WHO as a state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being, not merely an optimal state or absence of disease.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Physical exercise is any body movement produced by skeletal muscles that result in energy expenditure.
questions.explanation: False. Any bodily movement resulting in energy expenditure is physical activity; physical exercise is a subcategory that is planned, structured, and repetitive.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Reaction time is the ability to develop the gap between message receiving and responding or taking action.
questions.explanation: True. Reaction time measures the time elapsed between receiving a sensory stimulus and executing a muscular response.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Our level of physical fitness performance is not constant.
questions.explanation: True. Physical fitness fluctuates with training intensity, rest, nutrition, aging, and detraining.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: True or False: Muscle type is a factor that affects physical fitness performance.
questions.explanation: True. The ratio of slow-twitch (Type I endurance) to fast-twitch (Type II power/speed) muscle fibers directly influences athletic performance.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Who benefits from organizing a sporting event in one kebele, woreda, city or nation?
questions.explanation: Sport events stimulate the local economy, benefiting hospitality, public transport, retail marketers, and communities.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Who is benefited from gender equality in sports and society?
questions.explanation: Gender equality empowers women, improves family welfare, increases economic productivity, and strengthens the entire nation.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which one of the following is not the result of technology in sport?
questions.explanation: Fans are spectators and supporters; VAR, specialized sportswear, and fitness facilities are technological innovations.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Why do some athletes take prohibited performance-enhancing drugs?
questions.explanation: Doping violations arise from illicit attempts to enhance performance, recreational drug use, or misuse of prescription medications.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: What is not an accurate mechanism to determine our true level of physical fitness?
options: By looking at external posture alone
questions.explanation: External appearance or posture alone does not accurately measure cardiovascular endurance, VO2 max, or internal aerobic capacity.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which physical fitness component tends to naturally decline directly with increasing age if not specifically trained?
questions.explanation: Joint flexibility and muscle elasticity progressively decline with age without regular stretching routines.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: According to the caloric density per gram, which list is arranged in ascending order?
options: Carbohydrate (4 kcal) - protein (4 kcal) - fat (9 kcal)
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates and proteins yield 4 kcal/gram, while dietary fats yield 9 kcal/gram.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which one of the following is true about physical fitness?
options: When the level of physical fitness is improved, the resting heart rate decreases.
Our level of physical fitness does not vary from one person to another.
When you are fit, your energy intake is decreased.
When you are detraining, your performance remains constant.
questions.explanation: A lower resting heart rate (bradycardia of the trained athlete) indicates superior cardiovascular efficiency and increased stroke volume.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Body Mass Index (BMI) is calculated as the ratio of a person's weight (in kg) to his or her:
questions.explanation: BMI formula is weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters (kg/m²).

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which statement best describes comprehensive physical fitness?
options: The ability to involve in one specific type of sport event
The ability to develop a single motor skill
The ability to perform without effectively and efficiently through our daily life span
questions.explanation: Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks with vigor and alertness, without undue fatigue, and with ample energy to enjoy leisure and meet unforeseen emergencies.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: All of the following are skill-related components of physical fitness EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Flexibility is a health-related fitness component (along with cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, and body composition).

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: In 1 g of fat and 1 g of protein, how many total calories (kcal) are found together?
questions.explanation: 1 gram of fat = 9 kcal, and 1 gram of protein = 4 kcal; together they contain 9 + 4 = 13 kcal.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: Which pair represents health-related physical fitness components?
questions.explanation: Flexibility, cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, and body composition are health-related physical fitness components.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: What are the three primary energy-yielding macronutrients in human food?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids (fats) are the primary dietary energy sources.

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If a student has a weight of 100 kg and a height of 2 meters, what is their BMI?
questions.explanation: BMI = Weight / (Height)² = 100 / (2 × 2) = 100 / 4 = 25 kg/m².

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If a balanced dietary plan consists of 1,000 g of food daily and allocates 30% to healthy fats, how many grams of fat should be consumed?

questions.subject: HP
questions.question: If the same 1,000 g dietary plan allocates 57% to carbohydrates, how many grams of carbohydrates should be consumed?
